Here is a bash function and a test helper:

```bash
# clamp VALUE LOW HIGH: prints VALUE limited to the range [LOW, HIGH] (integers, may be negative)
clamp() {
  local v=$1 lo=$2 hi=$3
  if (( v < lo )); then echo "$lo"; elif (( v > hi )); then echo "$hi"; else echo "$v"; fi
}
# assert_eq EXPECTED ACTUAL: records a failure when the two values differ
```

Write a bash function test_clamp that checks clamp with at least 6 calls to assert_eq (for example: assert_eq 5 "$(clamp 5 0 10)"), covering values below the range, inside it, exactly at both bounds, above it, and negative numbers. Do not redefine clamp or assert_eq. Reply with a single ```bash code block containing only test_clamp.
tests:
AE='assert_eq() { if [ "$1" != "$2" ]; then FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi; ASSERTS=$((ASSERTS+1)); }'
OK='clamp() { local v=$1 lo=$2 hi=$3; if (( v < lo )); then echo "$lo"; elif (( v > hi )); then echo "$hi"; else echo "$v"; fi; }'
M1='clamp() { local v=$1 lo=$2 hi=$3; if (( v < lo )); then echo "$lo"; elif (( v > hi )); then echo "$lo"; else echo "$v"; fi; }'
M2='clamp() { local v=$1 lo=$2 hi=$3; if [[ $v < $lo ]]; then echo "$lo"; elif [[ $v > $hi ]]; then echo "$hi"; else echo "$v"; fi; }'
M3='clamp() { local v=$1 lo=$2 hi=$3; if (( v < lo )); then echo "$lo"; elif (( v >= hi )); then echo "$((hi-1))"; else echo "$v"; fi; }'
run(){ ( FAILS=0; ASSERTS=0; eval "$__GEN" >/dev/null 2>&1; eval "$AE"; eval "$1"; test_clamp >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "$FAILS $ASSERTS" ) }
read -r f a <<< "$(run "$OK")"
if [ "${f:-1}" = 0 ] && [ "${a:-0}" -ge 6 ]; then echo "PASS correct_impl_passes"; ok=1; else echo "FAIL correct_impl_passes"; ok=0; fi
for m in M1 M2 M3; do read -r f a <<< "$(run "${!m}")"; if [ "$ok" = 1 ] && [ "${f:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then echo "PASS kills_$m"; else echo "FAIL kills_$m"; fi; done
